name: The Equivalence Principle
statement: Gravity and acceleration are locally indistinguishable; all bodies fall alike.
meaning: In its simplest form, all bodies fall with the same acceleration in a gravitational field, whatever their mass or composition — inertial mass and gravitational mass are one and the same. In its deeper form, no local experiment can tell a uniform gravitational field apart from uniform acceleration. This was Einstein's guiding insight on the road to general relativity: that gravity is not a force like the others but a feature of spacetime itself.
mechanism: Because gravity accelerates everything identically, its local effect can be entirely transformed away by choosing a freely falling frame — something no genuine force, which acts differently on different bodies, allows. That universality is the signature of a geometric effect. Einstein's leap was to conclude that gravity is not a force but the curvature of spacetime: freely falling bodies follow geodesics, the straightest possible paths through a curved geometry, and what we feel as gravitational acceleration is that geometry. The principle comes in a hierarchy — the weak form for falling test bodies, the Einstein form adding that all local non-gravitational physics is frame- and position-independent, and the strong form extending even to self-gravitating bodies and gravitational experiments.

examples.text: Einstein's 1907 realisation that a person in free fall feels no weight — the seed of the whole idea, that free fall cancels gravity locally.

In a windowless chamber you cannot tell whether you are at rest in gravity or accelerating through empty space; dropped objects fall the same way in both, and float the same way when the chamber falls freely.

The MICROSCOPE satellite compared the fall of titanium and platinum masses in orbit and found them equal to about one part in a thousand trillion, the most precise confirmation of the weak equivalence principle to date.

variants.name: The weak, Einstein, and strong forms
variants.text: A strict hierarchy: the weak principle that test bodies fall alike, the Einstein principle adding local Lorentz and position invariance, and the strong principle extending equivalence to gravitating bodies — general relativity being essentially the unique theory that satisfies the last.

variants.name: Tests of universality of free fall
variants.text: The long line of experiments, from Newton's pendulums and Eotvos's torsion balance through lunar laser ranging and modern rotating balances to the MICROSCOPE satellite, tightening the bound on any composition dependence of gravity.

whyItMatters: It is the conceptual bridge from Newtonian gravity to general relativity, the insight that turned gravity from a force into geometry. That inertial and gravitational mass are identical — a coincidence in Newton's theory — becomes necessary once gravity is curvature. The principle organises how we test gravity and, in whether its strong form holds, marks the dividing line between general relativity and most of its rivals.

working.text: to simplify a problem, adopt a freely falling frame in which gravity locally vanishes and special relativity holds.
keep the weak, Einstein, and strong principles apart; confirming that bodies fall alike says nothing directly about the stronger claims.
remember the equivalence is local; over any extended region, tidal forces betray real gravity and cannot be transformed away.

limits: The equivalence of gravity and acceleration is strictly local. Over an extended region, tidal forces — the variation of a real gravitational field, as two dropped balls converge toward a planet's centre — reveal genuine gravity that uniform acceleration cannot mimic; these tidal effects are the true, non-removable signature of curvature. The strong form may be violated in alternative theories with a varying gravitational constant or extra fields, currently bounded by lunar laser ranging. Quantum tests with matter waves are an active frontier, and how the principle meshes with quantum mechanics remains open. Even antimatter was, until recently, an open question, resolved in 2023 when antihydrogen was directly observed to fall down, consistent with ordinary matter, though only to coarse precision.
misreadings: Gravity is not a force like the others here — the whole point is that it can be transformed away locally, which no true force permits. And the equivalence is not global or exact: it holds only in a small enough region, and tidal forces distinguish real gravity from acceleration over any extended one. Confirming that bodies fall alike, the weak principle, does not by itself confirm general relativity, since many rival theories satisfy it too.
origin: Rooted in Galileo's finding that free fall is independent of composition and Newton's pendulum tests of the equality of inertial and gravitational mass; raised to a principle by Albert Einstein from his 1907 realisation that a falling observer feels no gravity, which guided his development of general relativity by 1915. The weak form has been tested to about one part in a thousand trillion by the MICROSCOPE satellite in 2022.
